checks.note: Excerpt verbatim; the referendum is correctly treated as normative. Rationale matches e1 (one Firmus IPO pulled, not a broad freeze) and e2 (Meta Q3 2026 capex of $34.91B). The limitation about unreadable sources matches the packet. Open horizon/unresolved matches the reviews. Minor: what_would_resolve says 'financing failures... cuts and cancellations' where the contract says 'shortages... cuts, cancellations or failures'. The contract's exact support condition is shown in the criteria, so not treated as material.

Proposition, rationale, limitations and unresolved/not_applicable outcome are consistent with the contract and evidence. But the e2 excerpt is cut to 'all fully booked.', which drops the subject (A100 chips) and the attribution ('Intrator said'). That makes an unverified management claim read as a bare fact and leaves the quote unintelligible on its own. The excerpt should include 'Intrator said that CoreWeave's Nvidia A100 chips... are all fully booked.'

overclaims: The deadline is June 8, 2027, after the October 28, 2026 freeze.
checks.note: The rationale calls October 28, 2026 the 'freeze'. That is the evaluation date; the contract was frozen on 2026-10-29. Otherwise the June 8, 2027 deadline, not_due/unresolved outcome and e1 citation (NVCA/PitchBook, $108.5B raised through Q3 2026, available 2026-10-07) are correct. The limitations correctly note that fundraising data is not a measure of remaining capital.

Rationale ($31.91B net income; ~90% share; switching costs) and the supported outcome match. Citations are misleading. The e1 excerpt 'were both $1.30.' drops its subject (diluted EPS) and sits under a 'net income row' locator, so it could read as net income. The e2 excerpt cuts 'but AMD's ROCm platform has begun to narrow the gap', removing the source's own qualification and overstating its support.
